name: Sysmon Event IDs - Detection Reference
description: Complete Sysmon event ID reference for threat detection. Sysmon extends Windows logging with process, network, file, registry, and image-load telemetry — each event type maps to specific attack techniques.
source: CDSA Module 03: Windows Event Logs & Finding Evil
notes:
=== Core Sysmon Event IDs ===

ID 1  - ProcessCreate
  Key fields: Image, CommandLine, ParentImage, ParentCommandLine, Hashes, User
  Detect: suspicious parent-child chains (e.g. Word.exe → cmd.exe), encoded commands

ID 2  - FileCreationTimeChanged
  Key fields: Image, TargetFilename, CreationUtcTime, PreviousCreationUtcTime
  Detect: timestomping (attacker altered timestamps)

ID 3  - NetworkConnection
  Key fields: Image, DestinationIp, DestinationPort, Protocol, User
  Detect: beaconing, C2 callouts, unexpected outbound from system processes

ID 5  - ProcessTerminate
  Key fields: Image, ProcessId
  Detect: security tool termination

ID 6  - DriverLoad
  Key fields: ImageLoaded, Hashes, Signed, Signature
  Detect: unsigned driver loads, rootkit deployment

ID 7  - ImageLoad (DLL Load)
  Key fields: Image, ImageLoaded, Hashes, Signed, Signature
  Detect: DLL hijacking, injection (clr.dll/clrjit.dll in unexpected procs)
  → Config: must enable with <ImageLoad> rule in config.xml

ID 8  - CreateRemoteThread
  Key fields: SourceImage, TargetImage, StartAddress, StartModule
  Detect: process injection (CreateRemoteThread API)

ID 10 - ProcessAccess
  Key fields: SourceImage, TargetImage, GrantedAccess, CallTrace
  Detect: LSASS dumping (TargetImage = lsass.exe, GrantedAccess = 0x1010 or 0x1410)

ID 11 - FileCreate
  Key fields: Image, TargetFilename, CreationUtcTime
  Detect: dropper activity, malware writing files to disk

ID 12 - RegistryEvent (Object create/delete)
ID 13 - RegistryEvent (Value set)
ID 14 - RegistryEvent (Key/value rename)
  Key fields: Image, TargetObject, Details
  Detect: persistence via Run keys, COM hijacking, ASEPs

ID 15 - FileCreateStreamHash (ADS)
  Key fields: Image, TargetFilename, Hash
  Detect: Alternate Data Streams (malware hiding in ADS)

ID 17 - PipeEvent (Create)
ID 18 - PipeEvent (Connect)
  Key fields: Image, PipeName
  Detect: named pipe C2 (common in Cobalt Strike, Meterpreter)

ID 22 - DNSEvent
  Key fields: Image, QueryName, QueryResults
  Detect: C2 over DNS, DGA domains

ID 23 - FileDelete
  Key fields: Image, TargetFilename
  Detect: log wiping, evidence cleanup

ID 25 - ProcessTampering
  Key fields: Image, Type
  Detect: process hollowing, herpaderping

=== DLL Injection Detection Pattern (Event ID 7) ===
Suspect: clr.dll or clrjit.dll loading in non-.NET processes
  → PowerShell injected into notepad.exe shows clr.dll ImageLoad from notepad
  → Look for: ImageLoaded contains 'clr.dll' AND Image is not powershell/dotnet

=== Unmanaged PowerShell Injection (Event ID 7) ===
Tool: Invoke-PSInject
  Attack: powershell -ep bypass
          Import-Module .\Invoke-PSInject.ps1
          Invoke-PSInject -ProcId <PID> -PoshCode "<base64-encoded-PS>"
  Detection: clr.dll loaded by non-PowerShell process

examples.label: Get Sysmon ImageLoad events (ID 7) — DLL hijack detection
Get Sysmon ProcessAccess events (ID 10) — LSASS dump detection
Read Sysmon events from offline .evtx file
examples.command: Get-WinEvent -Path 'C:\Logs\DLLHijack\sysmon.evtx' | Where-Object {$_.Id -eq 7} | Select-Object TimeCreated, Message | Format-List

examples.label: Filter Sysmon events by multiple IDs
examples.command: Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational'; ID=1,3,7,10} | Select-Object TimeCreated, Id, Message | Format-List
